title: AI and clinical data to identify COVID-19 from CT scans
summary: In a test on 279 patients, a system combining CT scans and clinical information reached 84% sensitivity, compared with 75% for radiologists in the reported comparison. Retrospective study on data collected in China, without evidence of effectiveness in prospective clinical use.

evidence.tested: Trained on 626 of 905 patients and tested on the remaining 279 against radiologists: sensitivity 84% versus 75%, AUC 0.92, and 68% of RT-PCR-positive cases with normal CT correctly identified.
evidence.unknown: Intended for use when CT scans and clinical history are both available; CT alone may have limited negative predictive value; prospective clinical use not evaluated; specificity not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Combined chest CT findings with clinical symptoms, exposure history and lab results to identify COVID-19-positive patients.
